item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 11, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's your MJR Morning Brief.
As radio looks ahead to 2027, Wright Media Group’s Brian Wright outlines 10 resolutions for the industry, from reconnecting with local audiences to empowering employees and putting listeners first. His message? Radio must challenge old habits to remain relevant. Read all 10 resolutions at Media Jobs Report.
On the business side of media,
SiriusXM has named Anjali Sud its next CEO, effective January first. Sud currently leads streaming platform Tubi and previously served as CEO of Vimeo. She succeeds Jennifer Witz, who is stepping down after nearly 25 years with SiriusXM. Witz will remain as an adviser through 2027.
Turning to radio,
Urban One reported an 88-million-dollar third quarter, down 5 percent from last year. The company posted a 119-million-dollar net loss, largely driven by impairment charges. Radio revenue increased, helped by Dallas station acquisitions and political advertising. Urban One also plans at least 20 million dollars in annual cost savings.
In television news,
Carson Daly is adding another morning to his NBC schedule. Daly has been named co-anchor of Saturday TODAY, joining Laura Jarrett while continuing his weekday role on TODAY. He also remains Host and Executive Producer of The Voice. Find the full story on Media Jobs Report.
In media education news,
Mentoring and Inspiring Women in Radio is accepting applications for its third annual Erica Farber Mentorship in Management Program. Sponsored by WideOrbit, the year-long initiative helps women advance into radio leadership roles through executive mentorship and professional development. Applications are open through December 10. Find application details on Media Jobs Report.
In podcasting news,
Gwyneth Paltrow is bringing her lifestyle brand goop to a new weekly video podcast. The goop Guide premieres Wednesday on Spotify and Netflix, featuring conversations with guests including Zoe Saldaña, Ke Huy Quan and Rick Rubin. Audio episodes will also be available on major podcast platforms.
Turning to radio,
Cumulus Media's 93Q in Syracuse raised more than ten thousand dollars during October through its annual Taking Shots at Breast Cancer campaign. Led by Program Director Rick Roberts, the fundraiser has generated more than forty-six thousand dollars since 2020, supporting the American Cancer Society and breast cancer awareness across Central New York.
In media education news,
Performance Digital is helping prepare the next generation of marketers for an AI-driven workplace. Team members visited Midland University's Dunklau School of Business to discuss how artificial intelligence is changing marketing. Their message? Technology can help create content, but creativity, communication and human judgment remain essential.
Turning to music,
The CMA Awards are adding more star power to their 60th anniversary celebration. Luke Combs, Chris Stapleton, Megan Moroney and Lainey Wilson are among the newly announced performers. Brooks & Dunn will also receive a special tribute. The show airs live November 18 on ABC and Disney+, with Wilson returning as host.
And finally,
WildBrain is scheduled to report its full-year 2027 financial results on Thursday, November 12, at 10 a.m. Eastern. The company will host an earnings call as part of its financial reporting. Find webcast details and more upcoming media company earnings announcements on the MJR Financial Calendar at Media Jobs Report dot com.
For the latest media news, job openings, free tools and more, visit MediaJobsReport.com.
